LANE_KEEP_SECRET_ENV = "CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_KEEP_SECRET_ENV"


def _is_secret_env_name(name: str) -> bool:
    upper = name.upper()
    return upper in _SECRET_ENV_EXACT or any(
        fragment in upper for fragment in _SECRET_ENV_FRAGMENTS
    )


def scrubbed_lane_env(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    env: Mapping[str, str],
    executor: str,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Drop secret-pattern names from the lane child env, recording names (#832).

    Unknown executors keep nothing secret-patterned (fail closed). Only the
    executor's auth keeps and explicit `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_KEEP_SECRET_ENV`
    names survive; the receipt records scrubbed/kept names, never values.
    """
    keeps = set(_EXECUTOR_SECRET_KEEPS.get(executor, frozenset()))
    for extra in os.environ.get(LANE_KEEP_SECRET_ENV, "").split(","):
        if extra.strip():
            keeps.add(extra.strip())
    scrubbed = sorted(
        name for name in env if _is_secret_env_name(name) and name not in keeps
    )
    kept = sorted(
        name for name in env if _is_secret_env_name(name) and name in keeps
    )
    payload["lane_env"] = {
        "executor": executor,
        "scrubbed": scrubbed,
        "kept_secret_names": kept,
    }
    return {name: value for name, value in env.items() if name not in scrubbed}

    fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".result.", suffix=".tmp", dir=path.parent)
    temp_path = Path(temp_name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(dict(result), handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            handle.write("\n")
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())

def runner_liveness(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Advisory pid check on the runner that wrote this record.

    A lane's record read `timed-out` while its runner was visibly alive (#791),
    and the record could not say which reading was stale because it carried no
    process identity. `alive` is `os.kill(pid, 0)` at read time, never
    persisted, and only advisory: a pid can be reused, and a live runner on a
    terminal record is normal while the runner finishes retention after its
    final write. A `running` record whose pid is dead is the one firm reading:
    that record is stale.
    """
    pid = record.get("runner_pid")
    if isinstance(pid, bool) or not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0:
        return {"runner_pid": None, "alive": None}
    try:
        os.kill(pid, 0)
        alive = True
    except ProcessLookupError:
        alive = False
    except PermissionError:
        alive = True
    except OverflowError:
        alive = None
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno not in {errno.EINVAL, errno.EOVERFLOW}:
            raise
        alive = None
    return {"runner_pid": pid, "alive": alive}

import hashlib
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

_DEFAULT_BRANCHES = frozenset({"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"})


def _head_branch(repo_root: Path) -> str | None:
    """The checked-out branch, read from the git files (no process spawn)."""
    dot_git = repo_root / ".git"
    try:
        if dot_git.is_file():
            text = dot_git.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
            if not text.startswith("gitdir:"):
                return None
            git_dir = Path(text[len("gitdir:"):].strip())
            dot_git = git_dir if git_dir.is_absolute() else repo_root / git_dir
        head = (dot_git / "HEAD").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    except OSError:
        return None
    prefix = "ref: refs/heads/"
    return head[len(prefix):] if head.startswith(prefix) else None


def lane_token(repo_root: Path) -> str | None:
    """A name part no parallel lane shares: the task-run lane id, else the branch.

    Follow-up records were numbered by counting files in the lane's own
    worktree, so parallel lanes picked the same number and their merges
    collided as add/add conflicts. Every non-default branch yields a readable
    slug (the lane id for `task/<lane>`, or `branch` when nothing of the name
    survives slugging) plus an 8-hex hash of the raw
    branch. The slug alone is lossy (`foo_bar`, `Foo`, and a plain `foo-bar`
    all alias `task/foo-bar`), and any exception for "already a slug" names
    lets a crafted name take another branch's token, so two branches share a
    record only on a hash-prefix collision. On a default branch or a
    detached HEAD there is no lane identity, and the counter stays.
    """
    branch = _head_branch(repo_root)
    if not branch or branch in _DEFAULT_BRANCHES:
        return None
    token = branch[len("task/"):] if branch.startswith("task/") else branch
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", token.lower()).strip("-")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(branch.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"{slug or 'branch'}-{digest}"


def resolved_followup_record_payload(
    repo_root: Path,
    *,
    adapter: dict[str, object],
    resolved_title: str,
    artifact_date: Any,
    current_pointer_target_path: str | None,
    reuse_subject_key: str | None = None,
    scaffold_artifact_lib: Any,
    resolve_artifact_path: Any,
    resolution: Callable[[Path], str],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    def record_payload_for(title_text: str) -> dict[str, object]:
        return resolve_artifact_path.payload_for(
            repo_root,
            "debug",
            title_text,
            intent="record",
            artifact_date=artifact_date,
            adapter=adapter,
        )

    current_target = current_pointer_target_path or ""

    def usable(candidate_path: str) -> bool:
        if candidate_path == current_target:
            return False
        if (
            reuse_subject_key is not None
            and scaffold_artifact_lib.record_subject_slug(candidate_path) == reuse_subject_key
            and resolution(repo_root / candidate_path) != "resolved"
        ):
            return True
        return not (repo_root / candidate_path).exists()

    candidate = record_payload_for(resolved_title)
    if usable(str(candidate["write_artifact_path"])):
        return candidate
    token = lane_token(repo_root)
    base = f"followup-{token}" if token else "followup"
    for suffix in (base, f"{base}-2", f"{base}-3", f"{base}-4"):
        candidate = record_payload_for(f"{resolved_title} {suffix}")
        if usable(str(candidate["write_artifact_path"])):
            return candidate
    raise SystemExit(
        "resolved current debug artifact needs a fresh dated follow-up record, but every deterministic "
        "default slug for today already exists; rerun scaffold_debug_artifact.py with --title <specific follow-up title>"
    )

"""Event bytes survive every way a lane's executor can end, or the loss is recorded.

The carrier stamps executor stdout through a pipe (`StampingPipe`). The
v8.15.0 release critique (R1) found that close() could give up on the reader
and the caller then closed the sink, dropping bytes silently. These pin the
contract: everything written before close reaches the events log
byte-for-byte on normal exit, timeout, a signalled child and a parent
interrupt; a writer that outlives close, or a failing sink, is reported in
the capture receipt and never blocks the executor.
"""

class _FailingSink(io.BytesIO):
    def write(self, data: bytes) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]

    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(_FailingSink(), clock=lambda: STAMP)
    # Far more than a pipe buffer: a reader that stopped draining would block
    # this writer forever, which is how a failed sink would hang the lane.
    flood = b'{"type":"item.started"}\n' * 40_000
    writer = threading.Thread(target=os.write, args=(pipe.fileno(), flood), daemon=True)
    writer.start()
    writer.join(timeout=10)
    assert not writer.is_alive()
    pipe.close()

    capture = pipe.capture()
    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["error"] == "OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device"
    assert capture["received_bytes"] == len(flood)
    assert capture["dropped_bytes"] > 0

class _HungSink(io.BytesIO):
    """A sink whose first write blocks until the test releases it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.entered = threading.Event()
        self.release = threading.Event()

    def write(self, data: bytes) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]
        self.entered.set()
        self.release.wait(timeout=30)
        return super().write(data)


def test_a_hung_sink_cannot_hang_close_or_receive_writes_after_it(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "_CLOSE_GRACE_SECONDS", 0.05)
    sink = _HungSink()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=lambda: STAMP)
    os.write(pipe.fileno(), LINES)
    assert sink.entered.wait(timeout=30)

    pipe.close()  # returns although the reader is stuck in the sink
    capture = pipe.capture()
    sink.release.set()
    pipe._thread.join(timeout=30)

    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["error"] == "event reader did not finish before close"
    # The stuck write finishes; every later line is dropped and counted.
    assert pipe.capture()["dropped_bytes"] > 0
    assert sink.getvalue().count(b"\n") == 1

class _Tree:

def _rule(window: float = 100.0) -> tuple[rule_owner.ProgressRule, _Tree]:

    )

def _seed_git_head(repo: Path, head: str, *, worktree: bool) -> None:
    """Write only the HEAD the routing reads; a linked worktree's `.git` is a file."""
    if worktree:
        git_dir = repo.parent / "common" / "worktrees" / repo.name
        git_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        (repo / ".git").write_text(f"gitdir: {git_dir}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        git_dir = repo / ".git"
        git_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (git_dir / "HEAD").write_text(head + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

def test_debug_followup_lane_names_are_distinct_across_aliasing_branches(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A lossy slug let `task/foo_bar` and `task/foo-bar` (or `Foo` and `foo`)
    pick the same record, a plain `foo-bar` aliased `task/foo-bar`, and a task
    id spelled as another branch's hashed token aliased that branch; every
    lane token now carries a hash of its own raw branch, so only an 8-hex
    hash-prefix collision could still alias two branches."""
    names = set()
    plain = "foo-bar-" + hashlib.sha256(b"foo-bar").hexdigest()[:8]
    branches = (
        "task/foo-bar", "task/foo_bar", "task/Foo-bar", "task/foo.bar", "task/__", "foo-bar",
        f"task/{plain}",
    )
    for index, branch in enumerate(branches):
        repo = tmp_path / f"repo{index}"
        _seed_resolved_debug_pointer(repo)
        _seed_git_head(repo, f"ref: refs/heads/{branch}", worktree=True)
        names.add(Path(_scaffold_debug.payload_for(repo, title=None)["write_artifact_path"]).name)
    assert len(names) == len(branches)
    assert all("-debug-review-followup-" in name for name in names)
    assert any("-debug-review-followup-branch-" in name for name in names)  # task/__
